THE TIER IS NOT THE OBJECTION AND IS NOT WHAT HOLDS THIS. === CORRECTION, 2026-09-12, AND IT IS MY OWN ERROR RATHER THAN A CHANGE OF PLAN. This field previously read 'R12 DOES NOT APPLY AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ... claim_merge_slot.py is NOT among them', and the same false claim was written into the body of PR #11881. IT IS FALSE. scripts/ops/claim_merge_slot.py IS in check_pr_landing.py::LANDING_MACHINERY, so R12 applies and refuses this diff by construction. The error was a truncated read: I ran `grep LANDING_MACHINERY -A 40 | head -60`, which cut off before reaching the entry, and I reported the resulting silence as a verified absence - the exact failure RULE ONE names, that a search returning nothing is not proof of absence and a negative needs a denominator. The authoritative list, printed in full by importing the module rather than grepping it, is 11 entries: .github/actions/commit-to-main/action.yml, .github/pr-landing/*.json, .github/workflows/board-post.yml, .github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml, .github/workflows/pr-opener.yml, .github/workflows/stale-automation-sweep.yml, scripts/ci/check_automerge_trigger.py, scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py, scripts/ops/claim_merge_slot.py, scripts/ops/session_registry.py, scripts/ops/sweep_stale_automation_prs.py. The declaration is therefore corrected to `hold` and the arming file is DELETED rather than left beside a held PR. I am not narrowing the diff to escape R12 either: the whole point of the unit is that the grading must live in the tool every claimant already runs, so moving it out to dodge the guard would ship the reader and lose the mechanism. A human reads it once; that is what the rule asks for and it costs this change nothing. === THE DEFECT: R13 refuses to let a branch arm without a claim, so the claim half is a mechanism, while the release half is prose carried by nothing - measured over the last 25 commits touching session-board.json, ZERO ever wrote a cleared slot - and commit-to-main rewrites the claim on every automated commit across 27 workflows, so the field goes stale mechanically at the rate main moves (median 7.1 min between merges). THE FIX IS DERIVED, NEVER WRITTEN: four never-collapsed states (unclaimed / spent / live / undecidable) computed from merge_slot.branch, which every claim already carries, so nothing new is written at claim time and it works on every claim already in the history. OBSERVED LIVE at 2026-09-12T06:2xZ on the real slot: SPENT, branch gone from origin, 'Displace freely' - on its first run. THE LOAD-BEARING REFUSAL is that branch PRESENCE is not liveness: measured the same minute, 4 of 4 sampled lane branches merged four days earlier were still on origin, so presence grades undecidable and never live. IT NEVER BLOCKS THE WRITE - refusing to overwrite would invent a lock R13's own docstring says the field does not provide - and a crash in the report cannot take down the claim, which is pinned by a test because R13 fails an armed branch that does not hold the slot.
